title: ISO 14001 environment (add-on)
description: ISO 14001:2026 on the Core registers: environmental aspects and their significance, monitoring results and the concerns neighbours and others raise, with compliance obligations in the Legal register, environmental objectives, risks, incidents and documents in the shared registers, tagged ISO 14001 with their own views. Full adds emergency preparedness with tested response plans. Installs the Core registers (Full, for the Legal register) first. Written in our own words; no text of the standard.

levels.name: Starter
levels.description: Environmental aspects with significance, monitoring results and environmental communications, ISO 14001 columns, views and examples on the Core registers, the Environmental risk category and the audit-readiness dashboard.

levels.name: Full
levels.description: Everything in Starter plus emergency preparedness: the emergencies you could face, the response plan for each and when it was last tested.

sheets.name: Environmental aspects
sheets.description: What your activities, products and services do to the environment, under normal and abnormal conditions and in an emergency, across the life cycle, and which of those effects are significant and why.

fields.name: Environmental aspect
fields.description: The part of the activity that interacts with the environment: a discharge, a use of energy, a waste.

fields.name: Environmental impact
fields.description: The change it causes: water pollution, emissions, landfill.

fields.name: Severity
fields.description: 1 hardly noticeable, 5 lasting harm to the environment.

fields.name: Significance
fields.description: Significant when the score is 12 or more, or when a compliance obligation or the concerns of interested parties make it so.

fields.name: Approval step
fields.description: Where the significance decision is in its approval. Set by the Significance approval workflow, never by hand.

values.control: Closed coolant system, collected by a licensed waste carrier

items.name: Example: Packaging thrown away by customers

sheets.name: Environmental monitoring
sheets.description: The measurements that show how your significant aspects behave: what was measured, when, the result against its limit and what was done when it was over.

fields.name: Limit
fields.description: The highest result allowed by a permit, a law or your own target. Leave empty when there is none.

items.name: Example: pH of process water discharge, October

sheets.name: Environmental communications

items.name: Example: Oil spill in the yard reaches the storm drain

values.situation: A delivery hose fails while filling the oil tank and oil runs towards the storm drain.
values.response: Stop the pump, cover the drain with the mat from the spill kit, contain with booms, call the waste carrier, tell the environmental manager and the authority if oil reached the drain.
values.equipment: Spill kit and drain mat by the tank

values.likelihood_scale: 1 Rare: never happened here or at similar sites. 2 Unlikely: happened at a similar site. 3 Possible: happened here before. 4 Likely: happens most years. 5 Almost certain: happens several times a year.
values.impact_scale: 1 Negligible: contained on site, no lasting effect. 2 Minor: cleaned up within a day. 3 Moderate: reported to the authority or a neighbour complains. 4 Major: harm outside the site that takes months to put right. 5 Severe: lasting harm to the environment or a prosecution.

automations.name: Obligation evaluated as not compliant → raise a nonconformity
automations.description: Cascade: when the evaluation of an ISO 14001 compliance obligation finds it not compliant, a linked nonconformity tagged ISO 14001 is raised and the owner told, so the gap is closed and the evidence is there for the auditor.

actions.message: {id} {name} was evaluated as not compliant. A nonconformity has been raised.

automations.name: Obligation evaluated as compliant → next evaluation in a year
automations.description: Recurring evaluation of compliance: when an ISO 14001 obligation is evaluated as compliant, the date is recorded and the next evaluation set a year ahead, so Core's 30-day reminder comes round again.

automations.name: Obligation evaluation 14 days overdue → tell the environmental manager
automations.description: Escalation ladder: Core reminds the owner 30 days before an evaluation is due; when an ISO 14001 obligation is still not evaluated as compliant 14 days after the date, the environmental manager is told.

actions.message: {id} {name} was due for its compliance evaluation on {next_evaluation} and is still {evaluation}.

items.name: Scope of the environmental management system
How we find and rate environmental aspects

automations.name: Aspect review in 14 days → tell the owner
Aspect scores 12 or more → mark it significant
automations.description: Gate on the method: an aspect whose severity × frequency reaches 12 is marked Significant and the decision is noted on the item, so the significance rule in your method is applied the same way every time. A person can still mark a lower-scoring aspect significant for an obligation or a concern.

actions.message: Marked significant: the score is {score} (12 or more). Plan how it is controlled and submit it for approval.

automations.name: Significance approved → next review in a year
automations.description: Recurring review cycle: when the significance of an aspect is approved, the next review is set a year ahead, so every aspect is looked at again at least once a year.

automations.name: Measurement over its limit → raise a nonconformity
automations.description: Cascade: a monitoring result above its limit marks the measurement Action needed and raises a linked nonconformity tagged ISO 14001 with the figures, so the cause is investigated and a permit breach is not overlooked.

automations.name: Answer due in 2 days → tell the handler
automations.description: SLA clock, step 1: a concern from a neighbour, an authority or anyone else is answered within 14 days. Two days before the answer is due, the handler is reminded.

automations.name: No answer in 14 days → tell the environmental manager
automations.description: SLA clock, step 2: when the 14 days have passed without an answer, the environmental manager is told the next day along with the handler.

actions.message: {id} {name} was due an answer on {answer_due} and has none yet.

automations.name: Concern needs action → create an action
automations.description: Cascade: ticking Needs action on a communication creates a linked action in Actions, tagged ISO 14001 and due in 30 days, so what you promised the neighbour or the authority is followed up like any other action.

automations.name: Emergency test in 14 days → tell the owner

actions.message: Test the response to {id} {name} by {next_test}: run a drill or a walk-through and write down what it taught you.

automations.name: Plan tested → record the date and plan the next test
automations.description: Recurring test cycle: when a response plan is marked Tested, today's date is recorded and the next test set a year ahead, so every plan is tested at least once a year.

setup.title: ISO 14001 setup
setup.description: Four steps to an environmental system an auditor can follow, on the shared registers.

steps.title: Decide what applies
steps.body: Mark every ISO 14001 requirement applicable or not, with a reason for the ones that are not.

steps.title: Find and rate your environmental aspects
steps.body: List what your activities do to the environment, across the life cycle, rate each one and get the significant ones approved.

steps.title: Record what you monitor
steps.body: Record the measurements that show how your significant aspects behave, with their limits.

steps.title: Open a channel for concerns
steps.body: Share the concern form with neighbours and others who may be affected, and log what they already told you.
